rows.name: FAST_BACK

rows.name: PARITY

rows.name: DEVSEL

rows.name: DEVSEL_MEDIUM
rows.note: medium

rows.name: DEVSEL_SLOW
rows.note: slow

rows.name: SIG_TARGET_ABORT

rows.name: REC_TARGET_ABORT

rows.name: REC_MASTER_ABORT
rows.note: a transaction it mastered ended in a master abort

rows.name: SIG_SYSTEM_ERROR

rows.name: DETECTED_PARITY

rows.note: the self-test's result: 0 when it passed

rows.note: starts the self-test; the device clears it when it is done

rows.name: CAPABLE
rows.note: the device has a self-test

rows.name: BAR0
rows.note: A base address register's parts, as BAR0 has them: BAR1 to BAR5 have the same. A memory BAR and an I/O BAR read their bits differently, so the parts overlap.

rows.name: SPACE_IO
rows.note: 1 for I/O space, 0 for memory

rows.name: MEM_TYPE
rows.note: how wide a memory BAR's address is

rows.name: MEM_TYPE_32
rows.note: 32 bits

rows.name: MEM_TYPE_1M
rows.note: below 1 MiB, long obsolete

rows.name: MEM_TYPE_64
rows.note: 64 bits, with BAR1 the high half

rows.name: MEM_PREFETCH
rows.note: reading has no side effects: it may be prefetched

rows.name: MEM_ADDRESS
rows.note: a memory BAR's address, from its bit 4

rows.name: IO_ADDRESS
rows.note: an I/O BAR's address, from its bit 2

rows.name: Expansion ROM
rows.note: ROM_ADDRESS's parts.

rows.note: the ROM answers at its address

rows.name: BASE
rows.note: the ROM's address, from its bit 11

rows.name: Presets

rows.note: what a driver sets in COMMAND to turn the function on

rows.note: STATUS's errors: written back as 1s, they clear
